Beta-blockers reduce mortality in patients who have heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and are on background treatment with diuretics and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors.
The study aimed to compare the effects of carvedilol and metoprolol on clinical outcomes.
The study was a multicenter, double-blind, and randomized parallel group trial.
The study included 1,511 patients with chronic heart failure assigned to treatment with carvedilol.
The target dose for carvedilol was 25 mg twice daily.
The study included 1,518 patients with chronic heart failure assigned to treatment with metoprolol.
The target dose for metoprolol was 50 mg twice daily.
Patients in the study were required to have chronic heart failure classified as NYHA II-IV.
Patients in the study were required to have a previous admission for a cardiovascular reason.
Patients in the study were required to have an ejection fraction of less than 0.35.
Patients in the study were required to have been treated optimally with diuretics and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors unless not tolerated.
The primary endpoints of the study were all-cause mortality and the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission.
The analysis of the study was done by intention to treat.
The mean study duration was 58 months with a standard deviation of 6 months.
The mean ejection fraction of patients in the study was 0.26 with a standard deviation of 0.07.
The mean age of patients in the study was 62 years with a standard deviation of 11 years.
The all-cause mortality for patients treated with carvedilol was 34% (512 of 1,511).
The all-cause mortality for patients treated with metoprolol was 40% (600 of 1,518).
